questions.question: Describe the three main layers of the Earth.
questions.expected_answer: The outer layer is the crust, a thin layer of solid rock that we live on. Below it is the mantle, a very thick layer of extremely hot rock, some of which can flow slowly. At the centre is the core, the hottest part, made mostly of iron and nickel.

questions.question: What is the difference between rock and soil, and how do people use rocks?
questions.expected_answer: Rock is hard and solid, made of grains or crystals packed tightly together. Soil is the loose, crumbly layer on top of the rock, made of tiny grains of broken rock mixed with water, air and the remains of dead plants and animals. People mine rocks for metals like platinum and gold, cut them for building, and crush them for roads and concrete.

questions.question: Explain how soil, air, water and sunlight support life.
questions.expected_answer: Soil holds plants in place and gives them water and minerals, and it is a home for animals like earthworms. Air gives oxygen for breathing and carbon dioxide for plants to make food. All living things need water. Sunlight gives green plants the energy to make food and keeps the Earth warm, and animals depend on plants for food.
